\approx \pi2 p_y^{2}, \pi2 p_x^{1} \approx \pi2 p_y^{1}

\mathrmO^{+}=1 s^{2}, 2 s^{2}, 2 p_x^{1}, 2 p_y^{1}, 2 p_z^{1}

questions.q: The $F - Br - F$ bond angles in $Br{F}_{5}$ and the $Cl - P - Cl$ bond angles in $PC{l}_{5}$, respectively, are
questions.solution:
The geometry of $Br{F}_{5}$ is square pyramidal.

Here, the lone pair occupies the axial position and hence axial bonds will suffer more repulsion than equatorial bonds. Thus, the axial $Br - F$ bond length will be different from equatorial $Br - F$.

The geometry of $PC{l}_{5}$ is triangular pyramidal.

The axial bonds suffer more repulsions than equatorial bonds, so they are larger in bond length.

questions.q: Stability of the species ${Li}_{2} \text{,} {Li}_{2}^{-} \text{and} {Li}_{2}^{+}$& increases in the order of
questions.solution:
$ {Li}_{2}^{-} < {Li}_{2}^{+} < {Li}_{2}$
Bond order $∝$ stability of species
${Li}_{2} = \sigma1s^{2} < \overset{*}{σ}1s^{2} < \sigma2s^{2}; B. O = \dfrac{4 - 2}{2} = 1$
${Li}_{2}^{−} = \sigma1s^{2} < \overset{*}{σ}1s^{2} < \sigma2s^{2} < \overset{*}{σ}2s^{1}; B. O = \dfrac{4 - 3}{2} = 0.5$
${Li}_{2}^{+} = \sigma1s^{2} < \overset{*}{σ}1s^{2} < \sigma2s^{1}; B. O = \dfrac{3 - 2}{2} = 0.5$
${Li}_{2}^{+}$ and ${Li}_{2}^{-}$ both have same bond order, but ${Li}_{2}^{-}$& has more number of electron in anti-bonding molecular orbitals (experience more inter electronic repulsion) and hence least stable among three species.

questions.q:
Dipole moment of $\mathrm{HCl}=1.03 \mathrm{D}, \mathrm{HI}=0.38 \mathrm{D}$.
Bond length of $\mathrm{HCl}=1.3 Å$ and $\mathrm{HI}=1.6 Å$. The ratio of fraction of electric charge, $\delta$, existing on each atom in $\mathrm{HCl}$ and $\mathrm{HI}$ is
questions.solution:
From the definition of dipole moment,
$\mu=\delta \times d$
where, $\delta=$ magnitude of electric charge
$d=$ distance between particles (here bond length)
$\begin{array}{rlrl}\therefore& \delta =\frac{\mu}{d}\\ \text{ or, } \quad \frac{\delta_{\mathrm{HCl}}}{\delta_{\mathrm{HI}}} =\frac{\mu_{\mathrm{HCl}}}{d_{\mathrm{HCl}}} \times \frac{d_{\mathrm{HI}}}{\mu_{\mathrm{HI}}}\\  =\frac{1.03 \times 1.6}{1.3 \times 0.38}=3.3: 1\end{array}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Four diatomic species are listed below. Identify the correct order in which the bond order is increasing in them.
questions.solution:
Bond order $=\frac{N_b-N_a}{2}$
In NO, total electrons $=7+8=15\therefore$ Configuration of $\mathrm{NO} \begin{aligned}& =K K, \sigma\left(2 s²\right), \stackrel{*}{\sigma}\left(2 s²\right), \sigma\left(2 p_z^2\right), \pi\left(2 p_x^2\right) \\
& \approx \pi\left(2 p_y^2\right) \stackrel{*}{\pi}\left(2 p_x^1\right) \\
&
\end{aligned}

$\therefore$ Bond order $=$\frac{8-3}{2}=\frac{5}{2}=2.5$
In $\mathrm{O}_2^{-}$$, total electrons $=16+1=17
$$\begin{aligned}& \therefore \text{ Configuration of } \mathrm{O}_{2}^{-} \\
& =K K, \sigma\left(2 s^2\right), \stackrel{*}{\sigma}\left(2 s^2\right), \sigma\left(2 p_z^2\right), \pi \left(2 p_x^2\right) \\
& \approx \pi\left(2 p_y^2\right), \pi\left(2 p_x^2\right)\approx \pi\left(2 p_y^1\right) \\
& \therefore \text{ Bond order }=\f frac{8-5}{2}=\frac{3}{2}=1.5 \\
& \text{ In } \mathrm{C}_{2}^{2-} \text{, total electrons }=12+2=14 \\
& \therefore \text{ Configuration of } \mathrm{C}_{2}^{2-}\\
& =K K, \sigma\left(2 s^2\right), \stackrel{*}{\s sigma}\left(2 s²\right), \sigma\left(2 p_z^2\right), \approx \pi\left(2 p_x^2\right), \pi\left(2 p_y^2\right) \\
& \therefore \quad \text{ Bond order }=\frac{8-2}{2}\\
& =\frac{6}{2}=3 \\
& \text{ In } \mathrm{He}_2^{+} \text{, total electrons }=4-1=3 \\
& \therefore \text{ Configuration of } \mathrm{He}_2^{+}=\sigma\left(1 s²\right), \stackrel{*}{\ssigma}\left(1 s^1\right) \\
& \therefore \quad \text{ Bond order }=\frac{2-1}{2}\\
& =\frac{1}{2}= 0.5 \\
&
\end{aligned}$$

Hence, correct order of bond order is

$\mathrm{He}_{2}^{+}$<  $\mathrm{O}_{2}^{-}$$ < $$\mathrm{NO}$$ <  $$\mathrm{C}_{2}^{2-}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Match each of the diatomic molecules in Column I with its property/properties in Column II.
questions.solution:
- A. \(B_2\) : Has two unpaired electrons, making it p. Paramagnetic. The close energy levels of \(2 s\) and \(2 p\) orbitals lead to \($\mathrm{t.s - p}$\) mixing.
- B. \(\boldsymbol{N}_{\mathrm{2}$}$\) : Has a bond order of \($\mathrm{3}$\), so its bond order is \($\mathrm{s}$\). \($\mathrm{\geq 2}$\). It also has \($\mathrm{t . s - p}$\) mixing and can gain electrons, so it r. Undergoes reduction.
- C. \(O_2\) : Has two unpaired electrons, making it p. Paramagnetic. Its bond order is 2 , so it's \($\mathrm{s}$\). \(\geq\) 2. With electrons in antibonding orbitals, it can lose electrons, thus q. Undergoing oxidation.
- D. \(O_2^{-}\): Has one unpaired electron, making it p. Paramagnetic. It can both gain and lose electrons, so it q. Undergoes oxidation and r. Undergoes reduction.
The correct option is (3).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
${N}_{2}$ and ${O}_{2}$ are converted to monopositive cations ${N}_{2}^{+}$ and ${O}_{2}^{+}$ respectively. Which set is having correct statements?
$1.$ In ${O}_{2}^{+}$ , paramagnetism decreases
$2.{N}_{2}^{+}$ becomes diamagnetic
$3.$ In ${O}_{2}^{+}$ , the bond order increases
$4.$ In ${N}_{2}^{+}$ the $N - N$ bond is weakened.
questions.solution:
M.O. configuration of ${N}_{2}$ is
${\left(\sigma\text{1s}\right)}^{2}{\left(\sigma*\text{1s}\right)}^{2}{\left(\sigma\text{2s}\right)}^{2}{\left(\sigma*\text{2s}\right)}^{2}{\left(\pi\text{2}{\text{p}_{x}\right)}^{2}{\left(\pi\text{2}{\text{p}_{y}\right)}^{2}{\left(\sigma\text{2}{\text{p}_{z}\right)}^{1}$
B.O. of ${N}_{2} = \dfrac{10 - 4}{2} = 3$
M.O. configuration of ${N}_{2}^{+}$ is
${\left(\sigma\text{1s}\right)}^{2}{\left(\sigma*\text{1s}\right)}^{2}{\left(\sigma\text{2s}\right)}^{2}{\left(\sigma*\text{2s}\right)}^{2}{\left(\pi\text{2}{\text{p}_{x}\right)}^{2}{\left(\pi\text{2}{\text{p}_{y}\right)}^{2}{\left(\sigma\text{2}{\text{p}_{z}\right)}^{1}$
B.O. of ${N}_{2}^{+} = \dfrac{9 - 4}{2} = 2.5$
Hence, ${N}_{2}^{+}$ becomes paramagnetic so statement 2 is incorrect
M.O. of configuration of ${O}_{2}$ is
${\left(\sigma\text{1s}\right)}^{2}{\left(\sigma*\text{1s2}\right)}^{2}{\left(\sigma\text{2s}\right)}^{2}{\left(\sigma*\text{2s}\right)}^{2}{\left(\sigma\text{2}{\text{p}_{z}\right)}^{2}{\left(\pi\text{2}{\text{p}_{x}\right)}^{2}{\left(\pi\text{2}{\text{p}_{y}\right)}^{2}{\left(\pi*\text{2}{\text{p}_{x}\right)}^{1}{\left(\pi*\text{2}{\text{p}_{y}\right)}^{1}$
So B.O. of ${O}_{2} = \dfrac{10 – 6}{2} = 2$
M.O. configuration of ${O}_{2}^{+}$ is
${\left(\sigma\text{1s}\right)}^{2}{\left(\sigma*\text{1s}\right)}^{2}{\left(\sigma\text{2s}\right)}^{2}{\left(\sigma*\text{2s}\right)}^{2}{\left(\sigma\text{2}{\text{p}_{z}\right)}^{2}{\left(\pi\text{2}{\text{p}_{x}\right)}^{2}{\left(\pi\text{2}{\text{p}_{y}\right)}^{2}{\left(\pi*\text{2}{\text{p}_{x}\right)}^{1}$
B.O. of ${O}_{2}^{+} = \dfrac{10 - 5}{2} = 2.5$
$\text{B}\text{.O}\text{.} ∝ \text{Bond}\text{energy} ∝ \dfrac{1}{\text{Bond}\text{length}}$
